newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical hit with $20.5 million damages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical hit with $20.5 million damages.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp., a maker of surgical staplers and related products, said Thursday a federal judge has awarded $20.5 million in damages to Applied Medical Resources in a patent infringement suit.
The Norwalk, Conn.-based company said in May that a federal jury had found in favour of Applied Medical, which claimed that U.S. Surgical's products infringed its patent.
U.S. Surgical "will appeal the decision, which the company believes is totally unsupported by the evidence," Chairman Leon Hirsch said in a statement.
U.S. Surgical will reserve the full amount of the award, plus expenses, pending the outcome of the appeal, it said.
U.S. Surgical said there has been no interruption in product delivery because of ample inventory at distributors, and it has begun production of a new product outside the scope of the court's ruling.
U.S. Surgical's stock rose $1.125 to $32.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
